solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Software in my iPad here gets hacked

indicators.note: something hacked is cut up and broken into, so these words' letters are chopped and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone has broken into the software on my tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Software' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the definition; 'in' just joins it to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypermedia is a kind of computer content and program linking text, images and sound through hyperlinks, so it is a type of software.

clue.text: Mostly not certain about a southern male in US government

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word wraps around the next piece
mostly means not quite all of the following word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: if you are not certain, things are unclear
S is the standard abbreviation for southern
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man from the South serving in Washington is not quite sure of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLEAR loses its last letter to give UNCLEA, which goes around S, and M follows. The clue's 'a' is surface padding, since the A already comes from UNCLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the traditional personification of the United States federal government.

clue.text: Old spiritual leader good with Harris incensed leaders

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
with and and both mean together with

indicators.note: leaders are what go in front, so only the opening letter of each of the two preceding words is kept

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Kamala Harris has angered the leaders of a campaign, set beside a famous peaceful figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi, who died in 1948, led India's independence movement and was revered as a spiritual guide.

clue.text: Mix or leave a juice

indicators.note: to mix something is to stir it together, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink instruction: blend it or leave it as it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The article 'a' in front of 'juice' is part of the letters being mixed, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera is the gel-like sap from the aloe plant, sold as a drink and a soothing liquid, so it is a plant juice.

clue.text: In the end, riots will follow panic in American regions

parts.note: to be in a state is to be in a panic

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A warning that, after panic sets in, rioting will spread across parts of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will follow' places the single letter after the word for panic, as in 'getting in a state'.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is made up of fifty states, each a self-governing region of the country.

clue.text: A stink about Stone's first court decree

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first phrase wraps around a single letter

parts.note: taken as written
BO is body odour, a stink

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: Roger Stone's legal troubles create a stink over his first court order.
explanation.walkthrough: The S sits between A and BO. An ASBO, an Anti-Social Behaviour Order, was a British court order restricting a nuisance's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: An ASBO was an order made by a magistrates' court in the UK, so it is a legal ruling issued by a court.

clue.text: A shade of trumpery ultimately seen in US jail

indicators.note: a thing seen in a place is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the can is American slang for prison

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A colour typical of Trump-style flashiness turns up in an American prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue colour, one of the printer's primaries, so it is a shade or hue.

clue.text: Doctor subtotals around lunchtime for Trump, perhaps

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the time
to doctor figures is to falsify them, so the letters of the word after it are tampered with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
lunch is at one o'clock, and one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fiddle the accounts around midday on behalf of the president.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime as one o'clock, written as the Roman numeral I, is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolutist favours unrestricted power for a ruler, and the 'perhaps' marks Trump as one disputed example.

clue.text: In hearing, as is Donald Trump's trickery?

indicators.note: in hearing means as the ear takes it in, so we want a phrase that matches by sound

parts.note: Trump's hands are famously mocked as small, so he is slight of hand

explanation.surface: A dig at Trump's deceptions, with the phrase overheard at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke rests on the long-running gibe that Trump has small hands; 'slight' and 'sleight' are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is a conjuror's dexterous deception, and by extension any cunning trick or deceit.

clue.text: Like 'most' ballot boxes marine left by news chief

parts.note: a SEAL is a US Navy commando, a marine special-forces soldier
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A wry suggestion that some ballot boxes are left with a navy man by a newspaper boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'most' hint at doubts over election integrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballot boxes are normally closed securely to prevent tampering, so they are sealed.

clue.text: The Spanish notice blunders in political event

parts.note: el is 'the' in Spanish

indicators.note: blunders are clumsy mistakes, so the letters of the word before it are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spaniards spot gaffes during a political occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: An election is the vote by which representatives are chosen, the central event of political life.

clue.text: Breaking up can be brilliant

definitions.meaning: second meaning: British slang for excellent

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a remark that a split can be a good thing; smashing as 'great' is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing describes breaking violently, and in British informal speech it is also praise meaning excellent.

clue.text: Taking the mickey when Trump loses lead is comforting

indicators.note: Trump's leading letter is a T, and losing it means a T is dropped from the front of the phrase

parts.note: taking the mickey is British slang for mocking or teasing

explanation.surface: Mocking Trump when he falls behind in the polls is a comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening T is removed, since Trump's own lead letter is a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing pain or worry relieves it, so easing is soothing or consoling in the same sense as comforting.

clue.text: Idiot close to politician in race loves pressure

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written
COMP is short for competition, a contest or race
love is zero in tennis, and O looks like zero, so two loves are OO
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A fool near a candidate in an election who enjoys the pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is an old-fashioned word for a foolish or stupid person.

clue.text: Protest familiar Republican getting into office

parts.note: a familiar is a witch's attendant spirit, a demon

indicators.note: getting into something means entering it, so one letter goes inside the word that follows

parts.note: a station is a post or position, an office
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A well-known Republican taking up an official post sparks a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar' looks like an adjective for the Republican, but here it is a noun: a witch's familiar is a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a public march or rally voicing opposition, which is what a protest is.

clue.text: Contrary Don, not Dem, got in? Ruddy upset, of course!

indicators.note: contrary means the other way about, so the word for winning an election is turned round

parts.note: a candidate who got in has won the election

indicators.note: Dem stands for a Democrat, whose initial D is to be taken away from the name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the colour word runs back up

parts.note: ruddy means reddish in colour

explanation.surface: Against expectations, Donald rather than a Democrat was elected, and some are furious, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' attaches to 'got in', while the Democrat's D is stripped from Don; 'ruddy' is also a mild British swearword, adding to the anger.
explanation.definitionFit: No wonder is an exclamation meaning that something is unsurprising, just as of course says it was to be expected.

clue.text: Position taken by one close to falsification case

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: A stand taken by someone involved with a fraud case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken by' puts the position after the other two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example or occurrence, which is one sense of a case, as in 'a case in point'.

clue.text: Conflict with South coming to a Western capital

parts.note: war is armed conflict
S is the abbreviation for South
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: Fighting from the south reaches a city in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Western capital' looks like the definition, but 'a' and 'Western' are letters; 'capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

clue.text: Muslim leader left America, returning to meet Brown

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the preceding letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
US is the United States
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: An Islamic ruler departs the USA and comes back to see someone named Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is the sovereign ruler of a Muslim state, such as the Ottoman Empire or Oman.

clue.text: Fed up with vacuous Trump's flipping work? No further comment!

parts.note: someone who has eaten their fill is fed up, or full

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the two kept letters swap ends
vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word is removed and only its outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone sick of Trump's empty, flip-flopping output declares the discussion over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' here is literal, having eaten plenty, not annoyed; 'flipping' also reads as a mild British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is the punctuation mark ending a sentence, and saying 'full stop!' means there is nothing more to add.

clue.text: Fast to welcome a Democrat (finally!) with hidden potential

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the fasting word holds the other letters

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hunger strike welcomes a Democrat at last, someone with untapped promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but not yet developed or visible, so a latent talent has potential that remains hidden.

clue.text: She lost race? Bit of anxiety in capital of Georgia

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the city's name

parts.note: Atlanta is the state capital of Georgia

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A candidate who lost the Georgia vote feels some anxiety in Atlanta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Georgia' looks like a first-letter instruction giving G, but it is the whole city. In Greek myth Atalanta lost a footrace after stopping to pick up golden apples.
explanation.definitionFit: Atalanta, the swift huntress of Greek myth, was beaten in a running contest by Hippomenes, so she is a woman who lost a race.

clue.text: A despicable type in the ascendant? I'm outta here!

indicators.note: ascendant means rising, and in a down clue rising letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person

explanation.surface: A villain is on the rise, so it's time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ra is an informal northern English goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ra is a casual way of saying goodbye, the same leave-taking as announcing that you are off.

clue.text: Former First Family makes you head to Antifa marches

indicators.note: makes you head to means the letter standing for you is turned into another, so one letter is swapped

parts.note: the Trumps were the US First Family during Trump's first term
U sounds like you in text-speak

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The ex-presidential family turn up at anti-fascist protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' does double duty: the U changes to the head of Antifa.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk with heavy steps over a distance, so tramps is a verb meaning marches.

clue.text: Old fellow with weapon could cause World War Three?

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
aged means old
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: An elderly man with a gun might start a global war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' places the weapon first, ahead of the old fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the final world-ending battle, so a third world war is a fitting example of it.

clue.text: Foolish type in conservative group

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: There is a fool in the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: A clot is British slang for a dimwit.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a clot, in British informal speech, means they are stupid or clumsy.
